title: Mark base-failing checks pre-existing and judge each criterion anyway
summary: At verification, a check that failed in the job's baseline record (same name, failed on the base commit) is marked pre-existing and no longer fails the verdict. The verifier also runs when some other check fails, so every acceptance criterion gets its own result instead of none. Audience: the Athena operator reading verification records and verdicts.

defaults_applied.how: New unit and lifecycle tests; cargo test, clippy and fmt criteria.
Criteria run tests that exercise the verdict outcomes.
The fix is in the verdict computation and the verifier-skip condition.
A missing or empty baseline marks nothing pre-existing.
One focused change across verify.rs and run.rs.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Part 1 landed: the Baseline record is taken before the producer and held in closing.baseline in run.rs.
A check is pre-existing only if the baseline has an entry with the same name and passed=false.
The verifier now runs even when a non-pre-existing check fails, so criteria are judged; the final verdict still fails on that check.
Prefer using the check note over a new CheckRun field, to avoid a schema change under deny_unknown_fields.
No athena.toml or workflow change is needed.

acceptance_criteria.text: A unit test in verify.rs shows judge() passes when a check failed in the baseline and fails again at verification, with the failure recorded as pre-existing and not listed in the verdict's failure reasons. Run `cargo test -p athena-core verify`.

A unit test shows a check that passed in the baseline (or has no baseline entry) and fails at verification still makes the final verdict fail, with a reason naming it. Run `cargo test -p athena-core verify`.

A lifecycle test shows that when one check fails, the verifier still runs and every acceptance criterion in the verification record has its own result, while the final verdict still fails on that check. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test lifecycle`.

A lifecycle test shows a job whose base commit already fails a check, and whose change leaves it failing, can pass verification when everything else passes. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test lifecycle`.
The verification record marks pre-existing failures distinctly (for example in the check note), so a reader sees which failures were already on the base.
A missing baseline, or one with a note saying it could not run, treats no failure as pre-existing. An empty baseline is never read as success.
`cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` pass with no new warnings.
CHANGELOG.md records the new behavior in plain language for an outside reader.

out_of_scope: Changing how the baseline is taken (part 1).
Re-running checks or retrying flaky ones.
Changing landing, CI routing or budget logic.
departures: Slightly higher cost and time than the reference: the change touches verdict logic and the verifier-run control flow in run.rs, and needs lifecycle tests.
